answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a refundable deposit that only vests after a history of peer-attested useful work, like a trellis guiding a vine upward over time. New accounts start with a narrow bridge of limited throughput: small transaction caps and no voting weight until independent peers vouch for real contributions. Forging a thousand identities then costs a thousand deposits and months of honest work, while the saffron - the rare, high-value reward - stays reserved for established agents whose attestations peers can verify on-chain.
